correctness.rationale: Maximal-area square triangles have a full unit side as base; leading logarithmic mass arises at 24 ordered distinct-three-corner charts, while away from endpoints of opposite side the volume is O(h^5). Exact chart determinant gives H=1-2A=a+b+c+f+de-ad-af-bc-be-cf, and error 0<=a+b+c+f+de-H<=2eta(a+b+c+f). Independent symbolic expansion passes. Product-volume identity J_eta(h)=h^5/120(log(eta^2/h)+H_5) for local corners and 24 charts yields P(A>1/2-eps)~(32/5)eps^5 log(1/eps). After a,b,c,f and de rescaled by h and e=h^u, the limiting density on a 5-simplex is Lebesgue and u uniform independent, giving Dirichlet(1,1,1,1,1,1) times Uniform(0,1). The u near 0/1 extremes carry vanishing log relative mass; finite normal-form slack can be slightly negative without affecting weak convergence. Independent exact beta and determinant checks passed. Analytic localization/probability argument, not simulations, proves the limit.
residual_risks: Fixed three-point uniform-area square/parallelogram model, no finite-threshold independence, rate, or growing-sample extreme law.
